question: Nutritional counselling is best described as what kind of process?

options.A: A collaborative process between a nurse and a patient
options.B: A strict lecture on forbidden local foods
options.C: A rigid meal plan handed across a desk
options.D: A medical prescription written only by doctors

explanation: Counselling involves working together to address eating challenges rather than imposing a one-way directive. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h1)

question: Why must nurses consider economic constraints during nutritional counselling?

options.A: Patients cannot follow meal plans they cannot afford to buy
options.B: Expensive foreign foods are always required for good health
options.C: Budgetary discussions replace the need for physical assessments
options.D: Hospital management mandates the purchase of supplements

explanation: Recommendations must fit the financial reality of the patient to ensure practical implementation at home. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of improving nutritional health literacy in patients?

options.A: Teaching patients how to prescribe their own dietary supplements
options.B: Transforming abstract medical advice into actionable kitchen habits
options.C: Requiring patients to use precise gram scales for every meal
options.D: Eliminating all traditional staple foods from the local diet

explanation: Health literacy helps patients translate clinical concepts into realistic everyday food choices. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h2)

question: A diabetic patient is confused about portion sizes. What is the most practical nursing action?

options.A: Telling the patient to stop eating all carbohydrates completely
options.B: Demonstrating portion estimation using common household hand measures
options.C: Instructing the patient to buy an expensive digital kitchen scale
options.D: Providing a medical textbook on human metabolism to read

explanation: Using hand sizes is a practical, cost-effective method for patients to manage portion control without specialized tools. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h2)

question: Why do short-term restrictive diets frequently fail over time?

options.A: Patients receive too much medical support from community nurses
options.B: Local food markets stop selling healthy ingredients completely
options.C: Clinical guidelines prohibit long-term dietary modifications
options.D: They rely on restriction rather than sustainable habit formation

explanation: Temporary restrictions are difficult to maintain, whereas gradual habit formation supports long-term adherence. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h3)

question: How does involving patients in setting their own dietary goals affect compliance?

options.A: Compliance rises significantly because the goals feel personal and achievable
options.B: Compliance drops because patients lack professional medical training
options.C: Compliance remains unchanged regardless of who sets the targets
options.D: Compliance decreases due to excessive confusion over hospital rules

explanation: Personal ownership of goals increases motivation and the likelihood of successful adherence. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h3)

question: Dietary counselling acts as a primary defense against which type of health condition?

options.A: Acute bacterial infections requiring immediate antibiotics
options.B: Chronic diseases like hypertension and diabetes
options.C: Traumatic physical injuries from motor accidents
options.D: Congenital genetic disorders present at birth

explanation: Lifestyle counselling is a cornerstone in preventing and managing long-term metabolic conditions. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h4)

question: What is a major clinical benefit of stabilizing blood glucose through targeted nutrition?

options.A: Laboratory blood tests become completely unnecessary
options.B: Patients may require lower doses of prescribed medications
options.C: The patient is completely cured of the genetic condition
options.D: All dietary restrictions can be permanently removed

explanation: Effective dietary control can improve metabolic markers, often reducing the medication burden on the patient. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h4)

question: Which factor is NOT solely related to physical hunger when considering eating habits?

options.D: The body's immediate caloric energy deficit

explanation: Emotional and social factors drive eating behaviors independently of physical hunger cues. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h5)

question: Why must nurses address psychological triggers during nutritional counselling?

options.A: Psychological evaluations replace the need for physical anthropometric measurements
options.B: Emotions and stress often derail dietary intentions and cause emotional eating
options.C: Nurses are legally required to provide psychiatric diagnoses
options.D: Mental barriers are the only cause of malnutrition in hospital wards

explanation: Addressing emotional triggers helps patients find non-food coping mechanisms for stress and anxiety. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h5)

question: What is the ultimate aim of nursing interventions in nutritional counselling?

options.A: To ensure lifelong dependence on hospital clinics
options.B: To foster patient independence and self-care
options.C: To transfer all clinical responsibilities to family members
options.D: To eliminate the need for any further nursing contact

explanation: Empowering patients equips them with the skills to manage their condition independently in daily life. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h6)

question: How does building patient self-efficacy impact healthcare utilization?

options.A: It forces patients to seek private specialist care
options.B: It has no measurable effect on clinical visits
options.C: It increases the number of emergency room visits
options.D: It reduces frequent and costly hospital readmissions

explanation: Confident self-management prevents acute complications, decreasing the need for urgent hospital care. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h6)
